from.name: An Verstraete
from.org: OCMW Kortevoorde, a municipal social welfare centre

subject: How do we measure the case file coaching?
mail: We've agreed to coach new caseworkers on writing complete case files with a new template. The council wants to see results before renewing the budget. What should we measure?
snippets: 24 caseworkers, 9 of them in their first year.
Applications for support go to a review committee that decides weekly.
Caseworkers say the committee 'keeps moving the goalposts'.
diagnosis: New caseworkers submit incomplete files, so the committee sends them back and citizens wait weeks longer for a decision. The agreed fix is a template listing the six elements the committee needs, plus coaching from a senior caseworker on the first files.

gold.baseline: Share of files returned for missing information per caseworker group (first year versus experienced) over the last six months, from the committee log.
gold.behaviour: Files contain the six required elements, checked by a senior caseworker on a monthly sample.
gold.business_metric: Return rate and days from application to decision for citizens.
gold.collection: The committee's log of returned files and reasons, plus case system dates, reviewed quarterly.

traps: Number of files submitted per month.
Time spent writing each file, where more is not better.
data_available: Committee minutes log every returned file and the reason.
The case management system records application and decision dates.
debrief: The committee already writes down every return and why, which gives a precise baseline per group. The behaviour is a complete file, and the result that matters to the council is citizens getting a decision sooner.
